canonical_statement: For independent Bernoulli bond percolation on the nearest-neighbor square lattice with vertex set Z x Z, the infimum of opening parameters p in [0,1] for which the origin has positive probability of belonging to an infinite open cluster is 1/2.
domain_and_universes: Vertex = Int x Int; SquareLattice is the horizontal/vertical nearest-neighbor SimpleGraph; Bond = SquareLattice.edgeSet; Configuration = Bond -> Bool; p : NNReal with hp : p <= 1; all declarations are in Lean universe 0
hypotheses: The threshold set contains parameters p with a witness hp : p <= 1.
Each bond coordinate has law PMF.bernoulli p hp under Measure.infinitePi.
source_selection: Harry Kesten, The critical probability of bond percolation on the square lattice equals 1/2, Communications in Mathematical Physics 74(1) (1980), 41-59, DOI 10.1007/BF01197577. The title and bibliographic metadata identify the equality used here; pinpoint source-definition and errata review remain the later H audit and receive no H0 credit here.

boundary_policy: The bond model, unoriented square-lattice edge domain, product law, rooted infinite-cluster event, p in [0,1], and equality p_c = 1/2 are explicit. Infinite means escape from every finite vertex set through open-graph reachability. Absence of an infinite cluster at p = 1/2 is deliberately not part of this title-selected root and is retained as a distinguished mutation.
